topics.label: Course introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture series, outlines intended learning outcomes, and welcomes students from various academic backgrounds.

topics.label: Cancer as a genetic and developmental disease of differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cumulative genetic and epigenetic changes cause a breakdown in normal cellular differentiation, tissue architecture, and cellular models.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, malignancy, and nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics characterize the transition from benign to invasive malignant neoplasms through histological progression models and standard clinical naming conventions.

topics.label: Pathophysiological mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the mechanical, metabolic, and metastatic mechanisms through which localized and disseminated tumors cause illness and death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence and comparative oncology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the epidemiological frequency and mortality of tumor types across human populations and diverse animal taxa.

topics.label: Principles and practices of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the clinical rationale, diagnostic methods, and relative efficacy of screening programs across different cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing by recapping the lecture outcomes and giving instructions for upcoming practicals and sessions.
